documents.body: The Compass pilot reports agent deflection at 41% over six weeks across three support queues. Containment is counted when a ticket gets no human reply within 24 hours of the agent's final message. Resolution sampling covered 200 contained tickets: 63% were resolved without a reopen, 22% reopened within seven days, 15% went silent. The request asks Rae to approve general availability for all twelve queues starting November. Open questions from the pilot team: whether the 41% holds outside the three friendliest queues, and who owns the reopened tickets that currently sit with no queue at all.
documents.title: Compass support copilot: GA request

documents.body: Eval setup for the Compass pilot, written by Ivy. The agent answers from the help center plus resolved-ticket history. Guardrails: no refunds over $50, no account changes, escalate on legal or safety keywords. Metrics logged per ticket: contained (no human reply in 24h), reopened-in-7d, CSAT on contained tickets only. Known gap, flagged twice: nobody sampled whether contained tickets were actually resolved, so the headline deflection number mixes true resolutions with tickets that went quiet. Ivy's note at the end: containment is cheap to measure and easy to game; score resolution or do not ship.
documents.title: Compass pilot eval setup

documents.body: Tally billing search proposal: replace keyword search over invoices with vector search over invoice embeddings. Expected win: support tickets about finding charges drop by a third, and the billing team stops maintaining the synonym list by hand. Cost: one embedding pipeline plus rerank at query time, roughly $9k a month at current volume. Risk: retrieval quality on invoice numbers and exact amounts, which vectors handle badly; the proposal keeps a keyword fallback for numeric queries. The request asks Rae to pick the retrieval design before the contracts freeze on Friday.
documents.title: Tally billing search: vector proposal

documents.body: Northwind agent evals gate: the launch checklist requires task success above 80% on the golden set plus a red-team pass on prompt injection. Current numbers: 84% task success, red-team pass with two medium findings (tool descriptions leak internal paths; the planner retries destructive tools without asking). The request asks Rae whether the two findings block launch or ship as fast-follows with a two-week deadline. Ivy's position, recorded here: the retry behavior blocks, because it compounds silently in long-horizon tasks.
documents.title: Northwind evals gate decision

documents.body: Leads-only platform notes, October. The Q1 inference budget is not approved: finance capped GPU spend at the Q4 run rate, and two launches are competing for the same capacity. If Compass goes to all twelve queues in November, it takes the whole headroom and the Northwind launch slips to February. Nobody outside leads has seen these numbers. Theo's read: any GA approval has to sequence the two launches, and whoever announces the sequence owns the slip.
documents.title: Platform notes: Q1 inference budget (leads only)
